sections.h2: Where Daviess County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Every deed for Daviess County land goes through the clerk's legal recording department in Room 104, 212 St. Ann Street, Owensboro. It's open from 8 in the morning to 4:30. Call 270-685-8434 and press 3, or mail to that street address in ZIP code 42303.

City or country, a house inside the county line is recorded at this one counter. Staff will pull a document you can identify, but title searching is something to arrange through your closing agent.

Several payment types work, with a limit on personal checks. Pick yours before mailing a deed so the package doesn't come back.

  • Cash, cashier's check, certified check, business check or money order
  • Credit or debit card, with a vendor fee added
  • Personal checks only from in-state addresses with all information pre-printed
  • No counter checks

Make every check payable to the Daviess County Clerk. The clerk posts a legal recording fee schedule as a PDF on the county website. Ask the recording department for the current price of a deed, mortgage release or affidavit, since the amount depends on page count and document type.

sections.h2: How to format a deed so it's accepted
sections.html:
Daviess County follows the formatting standards the Kentucky County Clerks' Association adopted from the Property Records Industry Association. A deed that breaks them can be turned away at the counter, which pushes back your closing.

Daviess County document format rules
Document elementRequirement
Paper20 lb. white, no watermarks, 8.5 x 11 preferred, 8.5 x 14 accepted
PrintOne side only, black ink preferred, dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or similar
Margins1 inch all around, with the top 3 inches of page one left blank for the recorder
Not allowedStaples or binding, impression seals, colored highlighter

sections.h2: Deed tax on a Daviess County sale
sections.html:
KRS 142.050 charges the seller $0.50 for each $500 of price, rounding any partial $500 up. The clerk figures the tax from the value written on the deed and takes payment before it will accept the document, so write the full price in.

The clerk keeps 5 percent of what it collects and sends the rest to the county treasurer. Several transfers are exempt:

  • Deeds that only confirm or correct an earlier deed
  • Transfers between spouses, or former spouses in a divorce
  • Foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure
  • Transfers to or from a government body
  • Parent to child or grandparent to grandchild for nominal consideration

Most land records are open to the public, military discharge papers excepted. Come to the counter during office hours, or mail a written request that includes payment, a return address and a phone number. Mailed requests can take up to three business days. Staff will fetch a document you identify but won't research for you.

Walk-in copies cost $0.50 a page, or $1.00 for 11 x 17 paper. A certified copy is $5.00 for the first three pages and $0.50 for each additional page. Mail and fax requests cost $1.00 a page, and a certified copy by mail is $5.00 for three pages plus $1.00 for each extra page. Certified copies can't be sent by fax.

The clerk offers a free search through eCCLIX for individuals and businesses, with no daily limit once you create a free account. Deeds, mortgages, plats and wills have been digitized back to 1974, and the clerk is working to extend the index further back. Questions about the service go to the legal recording department at 270-685-8434, extension 3.

Your title company normally pulls the chain of title. You can run the same index yourself to be sure the last deed, any mortgage release and any easements are on file before you list.

sections.h2: Property tax jobs at the clerk's desk
sections.html:
Two property-tax jobs land with the clerk even though the sheriff bills the tax. First, the clerk receives assessment appeals. After a conference with the PVA, an owner files the appeal with the clerk before the office closes on the next workday after the May inspection period ends. The clerk also serves as clerk of the local board of assessment appeals and notifies the owner of the hearing date.

Second, unpaid bills arrive in the clerk's office after April 25 as certificates of delinquency. A 10 percent clerk fee is added, along with interest and a county attorney fee. From mid-July the clerk can sell the certificates, and the list must be published a month or more ahead of a sale. A seller with a delinquency should call 270-685-8434 for the payoff.

sections.h2: Phone numbers to save before closing
sections.html:
Each office in a sale answers a different question.

  • County Clerk, recording and copies: 270-685-8434, option 3
  • Sheriff's tax counter, current bill and payoff: 270-685-6133
  • PVA, assessment, exemptions and ownership records: 270-685-8474
  • City of Owensboro Tax Office, city tax: 270-687-8537

For assessments, appeals, tax rates and bill collection, the sheriff's office sends callers to the PVA and the clerk, so start with those two when a number on a bill looks wrong.

sections.h2: What to check before the deed is signed
sections.html:
Get your paperwork in order so the deed records on the first try and you avoid a second trip to Room 104.

  • Confirm that every prior mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Match the grantor names on the deed to the names on the last recorded deed.
  • Print on white 8.5 x 11 paper, one side, with the top margin left empty.
  • State the full price in the deed so the clerk can compute transfer tax.
  • Ask the sheriff's tax office at 270-685-6133 for the current bill, since property tax for the year is collected there and not at the clerk.

Daviess County was formed in 1815 from part of Ohio County and covers 477 square miles on the Ohio River, with Owensboro as the seat. It had 103,312 residents in 2020, 45,155 housing units and 68.1 percent owner-occupancy. A typical home is valued at $199,900 and typical rent is $918. The county issued 253 building permits in 2025, so new construction adds to the recorded transfers each year.

For a sale, the order of work is simple. Get the sheriff's payoff for the current tax bill, confirm the recorded releases, prepare the deed to the format rules, bring payment in an accepted form, and let your closing agent submit it. If the closing agent records electronically or mails the package, ask when the clerk will return the recorded copy so the buyer's lender isn't left waiting.

faqs.q: What is the Daviess County Clerk's phone number for deed recording?
faqs.a: Call 270-685-8434 and choose option 3 for document recording. The legal recording department is in Room 104 at 212 St. Ann Street in Owensboro.

faqs.q: How much does a certified copy of a deed cost in Daviess County?
faqs.a: In person it is $5.00 for the first three pages and $0.50 for each additional page. By mail the extra pages cost $1.00 each.

faqs.q: Does the clerk handle property tax payments in Daviess County?
faqs.a: No, not for the regular bill. The Daviess County Sheriff's Office collects current property tax at 270-685-6133, and unpaid bills move to the clerk after April 25.

faqs.q: Which party owes the Kentucky deed tax in a Daviess County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the grantor on the deed. Each $500 slice of price, partial ones included, costs $0.50.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Daviess County Clerk?
faqs.a: Yes. Send it to Daviess County Clerk, 212 St Ann Street, Owensboro, KY 42303, with payment made out to the Daviess County Clerk, and make sure the deed meets the paper and margin rules.
